summary.intent: Fix inconsistent sidebar icons in the web app — some were Unicode emoji/text, others were custom SVGs — by standardizing to one approach throughout.
summary.outcome: All 4 sidebar icons (folder, shared/link, bin/trash, settings/gear) were replaced with consistent inline stroke-based SVGs using currentColor. A PR was created and merged to main. A follow-up CI fix was also created to handle version-comment noise in the API spec verification step on the release-please branch.

repo: Sidebar icons were split between Unicode emoji strings in an ICON_MAP and inline SVG ReactNodes — the fix standardized to all inline SVGs with strokeWidth='1.2' and currentColor.

The release-please workflow bumps the version in generated TypeScript API client file headers (comment line '* OpenAPI spec version: X.Y.Z'), which caused the 'verify api spec' CI check to fail on release-please branches.
The CI api spec check already excluded info.version from openapi.json diffing, but did not exclude the version header in generated TS files — required a git diff -I pattern.
release-please-config.json was modified in the same merge window (expanded from ~25 lines to ~94 lines), indicating active release automation configuration work.

code.finding: ICON_MAP was changed from Unicode emoji strings to inline SVG ReactNode elements. Icons use currentColor and strokeWidth='1.2' for theme-consistent rendering.
.nav-item-icon changed from font/text-based styling to a flex container (16x16px) to correctly host inline SVGs.

git diff -I pattern for ignoring OpenAPI version comments was tightened from the broad substring 'OpenAPI spec version' to the anchored regex '^ \* OpenAPI spec version: [0-9]' to prevent accidentally suppressing unrelated diffs.

workflow: GSD quick workflow with worktrees can produce two separate worktree commits that need to be cherry-picked onto a feature branch manually — the executor spawned a second worktree for checkpoint approval.
The classifyHandoffIfNeeded Claude Code runtime bug may appear in executor output; check for summary file and git commits to confirm success rather than trusting the return status.
When fixing CI patterns (like -I ignore flags in git diff), verifying the exact byte format of generated file headers via grep is necessary before writing the regex anchor.

friction: Executor spawned two separate worktrees (one for the fix, one for checkpoint approval), requiring manual cherry-pick onto the feature branch rather than a clean single-worktree flow.

The release-please branch CI failure was a pre-existing systemic issue (version bumps breaking generated TS header diffs) discovered incidentally — not related to the sidebar icon task but required immediate remediation.
The initial git diff -I pattern was too broad and required a follow-up commit to anchor it properly.
open_items: PR #438 (CI fix for api spec version comment noise) was pushed but not confirmed merged — should verify it passes CI and gets merged.
The release-please-config.json expansion (25→94 lines) in the same merge suggests ongoing release automation work that may need attention.
No visual regression testing exists for sidebar icons — the fix was verified by code review only, not automated screenshot diffing.
